source_locators: Durrett PTE5 (2019-01-11) p. 244: definition of uniform integrability for a collection of random variables X_i, i in I; remark that choosing M with sup < 1 gives sup E|X_i| <= M+1 < infinity
components.notes: Definition, small-event control, notation E(Z;A), version convention and empty-family convention are present (lines 15-35). The source defines uniform integrability for an arbitrary collection of random variables (no integrability hypothesis) and derives L1-boundedness, hence integrability of every member, from the tail condition. The handbook (lines 17-18) defines the notion only for a family of real integrable random variables; the M+1 remark appears only inside the proof of thm:p15-ui-small-sets for an already integrable family (annex lines 6-7). Nowhere on the route is it stated that the tail condition alone forces integrability, so the source's unrestricted variant is narrowed, not preserved.
components.gap: Preserve the source's definition (Durrett p. 244) of uniform integrability for an arbitrary collection of real random variables: either drop the integrability restriction at lines 17-18, or state and prove at the definition that the tail condition alone forces every member to be integrable with sup_i E|X_i| <= M+1 < infinity (so the restriction excludes no uniformly integrable family and a family with a member of infinite mean is not uniformly integrable).

source_locators: Durrett p. 244: remark sup E|X_i| <= M+1; 'trivial example' of a family dominated by an integrable variable
components.notes: Both directions of the equivalence are proved (annex 5-20), with the empty-family and C=0 boundaries; domination (annex 22-26), finite families (26-27) and the counterexample to first moments alone (27-30) are written. The source's remark and dominated-family example are present.

source_locators: Durrett p. 245, Theorem 4.6.2 and proof (phi >= 0 any function with phi(x)/x -> infinity; examples x^p, p>1, and x log+ x; E phi(|X_i|) <= C for all i implies uniform integrability)
components.notes: The criterion, both source examples, the C=0 boundary and the added de la Vallee Poussin converse with an explicit convex Phi are stated and proved (annex 36-73). However the statement concludes that 'the family is uniformly integrable' in the sense of def:p15-uniform-integrability, which applies only to families of integrable variables, so the handbook's criterion presupposes integrability of every X_i; the source's Theorem 4.6.2 assumes only the moment bound and integrability is part of its conclusion. The annex bound E(|X_i|;|X_i|>M_eps) <= eps*C (lines 38-43) is never used to derive E|X_i| <= M_eps + eps*C. The source variant is therefore narrowed (or, read without the presupposition, has an unwritten step).
components.gap: Supply the source's Theorem 4.6.2 (Durrett p. 245) for an arbitrary family of random variables: state the moment criterion without presupposing integrability of the X_i and write the step that the moment bound forces integrability (E|X_i| <= M_eps + eps*C), or remove the presupposition at its root in def:p15-uniform-integrability.

source_locators: Durrett p. 244, Theorem 4.6.1 and proof; remark that uniformly integrable families 'can be very large'
components.notes: Statement over all sub-sigma-algebras; the 'very large' remark is rendered as 'needs no nesting or countability assumption' (lines 69-71). Proof written in full: small-event control of |X| via the tail-splitting estimate (replacing the source's dominated-convergence-by-contradiction step, with a stated reason, annex 95-97), Markov, conditional Jensen, defining identity on the G-event, uniform M, E|X|=0 boundary.

source_locators: Durrett p. 246, Lemma 4.6.5 and proof; p. 245 tools used in the proof of Theorem 4.6.3 (bounded convergence and Fatou in probability, L1 implies in probability)
components.notes: All five assertions proved with written steps (Markov; Borel-Cantelli subsequence; bounded convergence with the K=0 case; Fatou along a subsequence including infinite and zero lower limits; uniform event bound for Lemma 4.6.5).

source_locators: Durrett pp. 245-246, Theorem 4.6.3 and proof: clipping phi_M for (i)=>(ii), Jensen chain for (ii)=>(iii), cutoff psi_M for (iii)=>(i), enlarging M for n < n0
components.notes: Hypotheses match the source (integrable X_n, convergence in probability). (i)=>(ii) with the source clipping and the integrability of X via Fatou in probability; (ii)=>(iii) by the same inequality chain; (iii)=>(i) with the source's piecewise-linear cutoff written explicitly and the finitely many early indices handled. source_locators: Durrett p. 247, Theorem 4.6.9 (titled Levy's 0-1 law) and its continuation pp. 247-248: a line borrowed from Chung asking whether the result is obvious or incredible; the 'obvious' reading (best guess given F_n should approach the best guess given F_infinity, namely 1_A); the 'incredible' reading (tail event, Kolmogorov's 0-1 law); closing evaluation (p. 248) that the argument may not show the theorem is incredible but that it and later applications show it is very useful
components.notes: The mathematical content is present: event convergence a.s. and in L1 and the separate conditional-limit proof of Kolmogorov's 0-1 law, with written steps (annex 289-303). The entry cites 'thm. 4.6.9 and continuation' (line 174) but the continuation's commentary is absent from the route: no attribution to Chung of the obvious-or-incredible question, no statement of the 'obvious' heuristic reading as a justification, no presentation of the tail argument as the 'incredible' reading, and no statement of the source's evaluation of the theorem's usefulness. The source name 'Levy's 0-1 law' appears only as an index entry (line 175), not in the entry's text.
components.gap: Supply the continuation of the source's Theorem 4.6.9 (Durrett pp. 247-248) on the route: name the theorem in the entry as the source does (Levy's 0-1 law); state the question the source borrows from Chung whether the result is obvious or incredible; give the 'obvious' reading (the best guess of 1_A from F_n should approach the best guess from F_infinity, which is 1_A); present the Kolmogorov tail argument as the 'incredible' reading; and state the source's closing evaluation that this argument may not show the theorem to be incredible but that it and later applications show it to be very useful.

source_locators: Durrett p. 248, Example 4.6.11 (Y_n Bernoulli(1/n), Z_n in {0,n}, X_n = Y_n Z_n, F = sigma(Y_1,Y_2,...), E(X_n|F) = Y_n)
components.notes: Example 4.6.11 is reconstructed completely (B_n, C_n with X_n = n B_n C_n is the source's Y_n Z_n), with a.s. and L1 convergence, uniform integrability by direct tail computation, the conditional identity and a written two-sided Borel-Cantelli proof that B_n has no a.s. limit. The two added examples are proved. The example's opening general claim (uniformly integrable a.s.-convergent X_n give E(X_n|F) -> E(X|F) in L1) is available from thm:p15-vitali-convergence and item (1) of thm:p15-changing-conditional-limits with constant information (lines 95-108, 182-183); see defect_observations.

source_locators: Durrett p. 249, Exercise 4.6.2 (Lipschitz slopes form a martingale, converge a.s. and in L1, integral identity) and Exercise 4.6.3 (E(f|F_n) is a step function converging to f in L1; step-function approximation; remark comparing this with the bare-hands approach of Exercise 1.4.3)
components.notes: The mathematical tasks of both exercises are proved with written steps, including generation of the Borel sets, the completed-Lebesgue extension, the continuous extension to 1 and the integral identity for all 0 <= a <= b <= 1. The entry claims 'the complete source Exercises 4.6.2--3' (line 253), but Exercise 4.6.3's evaluative claim is absent from the route: the source remarks that this approximation is much simpler than the bare-hands approach of its Exercise 1.4.3, though it uses a lot of machinery.
components.gap: Supply Exercise 4.6.3's comparative claim (Durrett p. 249): state that the martingale step-function approximation is much simpler than the bare-hands approach of the source's Exercise 1.4.3 (the handbook's direct step-approximation route) but relies on substantial machinery, so that the entry's promise of the complete Exercises 4.6.2-3 is met.

source_locators: Durrett p. 248, Exercise 4.6.1: model Y_i = Z_i + theta; statistical reading for normal(0,1) Z_i (a sample from a normal population with variance 1 and unknown mean); definitions of the prior distribution (law of theta) and the posterior distribution P(theta in . | Y_1,...,Y_n) after n observations; claim E(theta|Y_1,...,Y_n) -> theta a.s.

The exercise's statistical reading and definitions are absent from the route: the entry says only that the theorem applies to normal (0,1) noise and uses 'prior variable' and 'posterior consistency' (lines 266-268) without stating that the normal case is a sample from a normal population with variance 1 and unknown mean, that the distribution of theta is called the prior distribution, or that P(theta in . | Y_1,...,Y_n) is called the posterior distribution after n observations.
components.gap: Supply Exercise 4.6.1's statistical reading and definitions (Durrett p. 248): that with normal(0,1) noise the observations are a sample from a normal population with variance 1 and unknown mean; that the distribution of theta is the prior distribution; and that P(theta in . | Y_1,...,Y_n) is the posterior distribution after n observations (so that E(theta|Y_1,...,Y_n) is read as the posterior mean whose convergence the entry proves).
